Abstract:

Accurate and reliable electric current measurement is essential for smart home systems,energy monitoring platforms, and industrial control applications. &nbspMost domestic andcommercial electrical appliances are powered through cables consisting of either single-wireconductors or two-wire power cords. This research presents the design, analysis, andexperimental validation of coreless and contactless current sensing techniques for bothsingle-wire conductors and two-wire power cables, thereby addressing the practicallimitations of existing approaches. &nbspConventional single-wire current sensing methodstypically require complete circumferential (360◦) access around a straight and centrallyaligned conductor. These techniques are highly sensitive to conductor misalignment andsensor tilt, leading to substantial measurement errors under non-ideal installation conditions.
To overcome these limitations, a nonintrusive current probe configuration is proposed in which magnetic sensors are arranged in an isosceles right-angle geometry. This arrangementsignificantly reduces sensitivity to tilt caused by either the conductor or the sensing unit,while eliminating the need for full circumferential access. The proposed configurationenables accurate current measurement under practical mounting constraints. Althoughthe tilt-insensitive method improves robustness, it does not address errors arising fromoff-centered conductor placement or interference from external magnetic fields. To mitigatethese effects, a yokeless circular array current probe incorporating four magnetic sensorsis developed. The symmetrical sensor arrangement ensures that the measured currentremains independent of conductor position and diameter within the sensing region. Thisconfiguration effectively compensates for positional offsets and enhances measurementstability. In real-worldresidentialandindustrialenvironments,electricalloadsarepredominantlysupplied through two-wire power cords carrying oppositely directed currents. Existingsingle-wire sensing techniques are ineffective in such cases due to magnetic fieldcancellation within the cable geometry. Furthermore, circular sensor arrays placed aroundtwo-wire cords result in near-zero net magnetic flux because of opposing magnetic fields.
To address this challenge, a compact and coreless current-sensing method for two-wire power cords is proposed. The developed probe requires only partial spatial access aroundthe cable and does not rely on a full circumferential enclosure. The proposed two-wiresensing technique achieves accurate current measurement while remaining insensitive tohorizontalalignmentvariationsandwithoutrequiringpriorknowledgeoftheinternalcablegeometry. Unlike conventional methods, the proposed approach is independent of conductorsize, cross-sectional area, and inter-conductor spacing, thereby eliminating the need forrepeated calibration across different cable types. Finite Element Method (FEM) analysis isconducted to investigate magnetic field distributions and validate the sensing configurations. Experimental results demonstrate measurement errors close to 1% for single-wire and circular array configurations and below 1.5% for two-wire power cord measurements.These results confirm the suitability of the proposed coreless current sensing techniques for practical deployment in smart homes, energy monitoring, and industrial applications.
